Head Coach JESSE MINTER Offensive Coordinator DECLAN DOYLE Defensive Coordinator ANTHONY WEAVER OFF SEASON CHANGES Baltimore had a clear focus to improve defensively, and they’ve added 10 Pro Bowls of pass rusher experience between Trey Hendrickson and Calais Campbell, then drafted Zion Young 45th overall. The Ravens actually traded for 5x Pro Bowler Maxx Crosby but the deal then fell through after a failed medical. They also signed new head coach Jesse Minter, previously the Chargers’ DC. The Chargers finished in the top 10 in sacks in both Minter’s seasons as DC. QUARTERBACKS Lamar Jackson is still the heartbeat of this team and Baltimore will be hoping he can get back to his best after an injury-riddled 2025 campaign. Lamar started 13 games last season but was clearly not at full health, ending the year with 21 passing TDs and just 2 rushing TDs. They were clearly protecting him at points last season, with Derrick Henry taking most of the goal line carries and far less frequent designed run plays for Lamar. Lamar is still just 29 years old and in his prime, so I expect him to return to the MVP conversation if he stays healthy. Tyler Huntley signed a new two-year deal and will remain as the backup. RUNNING BACKS Derrick Henry is still the workhorse RB for the Ravens, but the big question is how long he can maintain his elite efficiency. Henry will turn 33 this season and he’s had 300+ carries in back-to-back years with the Ravens. Henry had 1595 rushing yards last year with 16 rushing TDs, another incredible season. He did have some fumble issues though, losing the ball a career-high 3 times last year. No back with 100-plus carries has topped 4.5 yards per carry at age 35-plus since 2016, but Henry still has a couple of years before he gets there. Justice Hill remains the third-down and change of pace back behind Henry. There isn’t a lot of depth in this backfield but the Ravens are relying on Henry to maintain his performance going into his 11th NFL season. RECEIVERS The Ravens lost tight end Isaiah Likely to the Giants which means veteran Mark Andrews regains the role as TE1. Andrews is still only 30 years old and the Ravens will hope he can recapture the form he showed back in 2021 and 2022 where he had 70+ receptions both years. At wide receiver, Zay Flowers is the undisputed WR1 and is coming off back to back Pro Bowl seasons. He had 1200 receiving yards last year along with 5 TDs. Flowers just signed a huge extension in the offseason which will make him one of the highest paid receivers in the NFL. I don’t think he’s rated in those top receivers, so maybe he will have a point to prove to get himself there. There have been a lot of positive reports coming out about rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane who was drafted with pick 80. He is an athletic beast at over 6 foot 3 and could have a decent role from Week 1. DEFENSE The Ravens’ defense fell off last season, especially in the pass rush. They placed 28th overall in both team pass rush win rate and sacks (30 total) in 2025. Enter Trey Hendrickson and Calais Campbell this year and that bottom-five defense should be back to top-10 territory. Rookie linebacker Zion Young should also help in that area. Their secondary is one of the best in the league, led by Kyle Hamilton, Malaki Starks and Chidobe Awuzie. If everything clicks in Jesse Minter’s new scheme, the Ravens will have a very good defense. PREDICTIONS 11-6 I have the Ravens narrowly winning the AFC North over the Bengals. I think the Steelers will be slightly less competitive but the Ravens should return to the top of the division with better health and a revamped defense. Last season, Cincinnati's defense couldn't get stops, forcing Joe Burrow to play from behind often and limiting a dangerous offense that finished with the fourth-fewest rushing yards per game (93.6). This year, Burrow is healthy, fully loaded, and a top-two MVP favorite, with Chase Brown entrenched as RB1 after a breakout season and Ja'Marr Chase leading one of the NFL's best receiver rooms. Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki add further depth. With a revamped front seven featuring Lawrence, Mafe, and Allen alongside young talents like Shemar Stewart, the defense should finally support the offense. Head Coach ZAC TAYLOR Offensive Coordinator DAN PITCHER Defensive Coordinator AL GOLDEN OFF SEASON CHANGES The Bengals finally took some action to improve their defense, which has been a handbrake on their last few seasons. They spent over $126 million in new contracts, landing safety Bryan Cook, edge rusher Boye Mafe and defensive lineman Jonathan Allen. Then they doubled down and landed former Giants’ defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence. All this spending was helped by Joe Burrow restructuring his contract to free up some cap space. The offense remained largely untouched and we know that they can put up scores when all healthy. QUARTERBACKS When Burrow is healthy, he is a top QB in the NFL. In four of his past five seasons, more than 6% of his total pass attempts have been touchdowns. Most other QBs are in the 4-4.5% range. Burrow is currently the second favorite for MVP and it’s hard to argue against him having a great season. The Bengals’ defense could barely get a stop last year which often meant Burrow was forced to play from behind or not be on the field for long periods. That should change this year and he is stacked with talent around him. I wouldn’t be surprised if he returns to the heights of 2024 where he had 43 TD passes and nearly 5000 passing yards. He’s in his prime at 29 years old and the Bengals are going all-in. Joe Flacco returns as arguably the best backup in the NFL. Despite his age he can still sling it. RUNNING BACKS The Bengals had the fourth fewest rushing yards per game in 2025 with just 93.6 per game. Some of that comes down to game script, where they were often playing from behind. It’s also a pass-heavy team with Joe Burrow at QB. Chase Brown is the undisputed RB1 after a breakout 2025 season. He had 1019 rushing yards along with 437 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns for the year. Despite being a smaller back he’s super explosive and can damage teams on the ground and through the air. This will be the final year of his rookie contract, so he’s got plenty of motivation to perform and earn himself a pay rise. His season rushing line is set at 850.5 yards which is very low but I also like his receiving props. Samaje Perine is the more bulldozing back and is often used in short yardage situations. RECEIVERS This is one of the most stacked receiver rooms in the NFL, led by arguably the best receiver in the league, Ja’Marr Chase. He’s put up over 1000 receiving yards in all five of his seasons as a pro and is coming off a 1412 yard season with 8 TDs. Chase is the second-highest paid receiver in the league, earning over $40 million per season. There’s not much more that needs to be said about him, he’s an elite weapon for Joe Burrow and he can do it all. Tee Higgins would be WR1 on a lot of other teams but plays second fiddle to Chase. Higgins had a down year by his standards in 2025, finishing with just one game of 100+ yards. Andrei Iosivas, Dohnte Meyers and tight end Mike Gesicki all complement the two stars nicely. Expect big numbers from this unit in 2026, especially if Burrow stays healthy and their defense can get them on the field more often. DEFENSE The Bengals have completely revamped their defense and their season will likely come down to how it performs. Dexter Lawrence anchors the interior after arriving via trade and he gives them a serious force up front for the first time in years. The additions of Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen give Cincinnati proven pass-rush and run-stopping experience too. Bryan Cook is a solid safety and fills the missing piece next to Jordan Battle. They’ve also got a young core of Shemar Stewart, DJ Turner II and Barrett Carter who should benefit from the veteran experience around them. PREDICTIONS 10-7 I have the Bengals making the playoffs but narrowly missing out on the AFC North title to the Ravens. It’s really all on their defense this year, if they can make some good improvements then this team will win more games. They could go deep in playoffs if it all clicks. Basically if he plays a full season, he clears this. All reports are that he is in great shape and feeling motivated, so I'm taking the over. Head Coach TODD MONKEN Offensive Coordinator TRAVIS SWITZER Defensive Coordinator MIKE RUTENBERG OFF SEASON CHANGES Big changes all over the place for the Browns after firing Kevin Stefanski and replacing him with Todd Monken as HC. The bombshell trade of the offseason was sending Myles Garrett to the Rams for Jared Verse and a load of draft capital. He’s a massive loss for this defense, as well as defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz who resigned after missing out on the head coaching job. The Browns invested heavily in their offense through the draft, taking two receivers in the first two rounds and OT Spencer Fano with pick 9. QUARTERBACKS The Browns had the second-fewest passing yards per game last season and have now committed to Deshaun Watson as their Week 1 starter. Watson has recovered from his achilles tear that wiped out his whole 2025 season and it’s his final chance to prove himself in the last year of his contract. He restructured his deal which freed up $36 million in cap space for the Browns. Shedeur Sanders is a fan favorite and led the Browns to a few wins last year, but his 7-10 TD to interception ratio wasn’t overly convincing. Dillon Gabriel started six games in his rookie season but it seems he’s third in the pecking order going into 2026. RUNNING BACKS The Browns’ rushing attack was sixth-worst in the NFL last season, but Quinshon Judkins emerged as a solid prospect throughout the season. He suffered a pretty horrific fractured leg and dislocated ankle in December but is reportedly healthy and ready to go for this season. Prior to his injury he had 827 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns which had him in contention for OROTY. The worrying thing was that he averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, but a lot of that came down to the Browns’ weak offensive line and poor passing game. RECEIVERS The Browns had just two players with more than 600 receiving yards in 2025 – rookie tight end Harold Fannin Jr (731 yards) and WR Jerry Jeudy (602). They’ve gone heavy in the draft to improve their receiver room, taking WR KC Concepcion with pick 24 and WR Denzel Boston with pick 39. They’re both exciting prospects with Concepcion averaging 15.1 yards per catch and 9 touchdowns at Texas A&M last season. Boston had 881 yards and 11 touchdowns for Washington in his final college year too. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr looks like a foundational piece and he’ll be thrown into an even bigger role now that David Njoku is gone. The talent is there now for the Browns, but the bigger issue here is who is throwing them the ball. DEFENSE Defense wasn’t the issue for the Browns last year, with one of the highest rated units in the league. Unfortunately they lost both their best player Myles Garrett and their defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz. The bombshell trade with Garrett did bring Jared Verse to Cleveland and he’s an exciting prospect, recording 7.5 sacks for the Rams last season. He’s just 25 years old and is a nice replacement at defensive end. The Browns are still stacked with talent, with the likes of Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell, Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham. This should still be a top-15 defense but it’s going to be a big task replacing a coordinator and reigning DPOTY in the same off-season. PREDICTIONS 4-13 Another tough year ahead for the Browns in my opinion. This will be Deshaun Watson’s final year of his contract but I wouldn’t be surprised to see at least three different starting QBs throughout the year. Their defense is not as good without Garrett and they’ll struggle to win many games. Pittsburgh also traded for receiver Michael Pittman to pair with DK Metcalf and added cornerback Jamel Dean in a huge free-agent deal. Last season, the Steelers won their division largely on the back of a strong defense, though their passing attack ranked poorly in efficiency. This year, Rico Dowdle joins Jaylen Warren in a shared backfield, while Metcalf and Pittman give Rodgers reliable short-range targets. The defense remains stacked with TJ Watt, Cam Heyward, and now Dean anchoring the secondary. Head Coach MIKE MCCARTHY Offensive Coordinator BRIAN ANGELICHIO Defensive Coordinator PATRICK GRAHAM OFF SEASON CHANGES Pittsburgh spent the offseason publicly courting Aaron Rodgers to run it back for one more season, and they succeeded. He’s announced this will be his final year in the NFL. The big change is at head coach – with Mike McCarthy taking the reins after Mike Tomlin stepped down after 19 seasons with the team. McCarthy has over 290 wins in the NFL and coached the Packers (with Rodgers as QB) between 2006-2018 and the Cowboys between 2020-2024. The Steelers also traded for veteran receiver Michael Pittman and he’ll be a nice addition alongside DK Metcalf. Defensively, they added cornerback Jamel Dean in one of their largest free-agent contracts ever. QUARTERBACKS Aaron Rodgers returns for his final NFL season on a one-year deal worth up to $25 million. The Steelers placed an unrestricted free-agent tender on him to keep the door closed to other teams. Rodgers still has a decent arm and recorded 3,322 passing yards last season to go with 24 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. The worrying stat for Rodgers and the Steelers is that 76% of his attempts travelled under 10 yards last season – the highest rate in the league. It’ll be interesting to see if Mike McCarthy trusts him to air it out more this season. He does have two really solid receivers in Metcalf and Pittman at his disposal. Rodgers wants to win one more Super Bowl but I really don’t see that happening this year. RUNNING BACKS The Steelers lost Kenneth Gainwell in free agency but replaced him with former Panthers’ RB Rico Dowdle. Dowdle has back to back seasons with 1000+ rushing yards and had a couple of massive games last year with 206 yards and 183 yards in back to back weeks. His efficiency dipped later in the season but he’s probably an upgrade on Gainwell. Dowdle will be fighting for the starting RB position with Jaylen Warren. Warren had a very solid 2025 campaign, putting up 958 rushing yards and 333 receiving yards. He was Rodgers’ favorite dump-off option last year with 2+ targets in all but two games. This should be a solid backfield and I expect the Steelers to lean on the run a lot this season with Rodgers being more of a game manager. RECEIVERS Pittsburgh made a receiver trade for the second straight year, bringing in Michael Pittman from the Colts on a three year, $59 million deal after doing similar for DK Metcalf in 2025. Pittman looks like a good fit for where this passing game lives – short options. He averaged just 8.1 air yards per target in his best season, which lines up nicely with Rodgers’ increasingly short-range approach in the later stages of his career. DK Metcalf should still be WR1 and is the deeper threat to pair with Pittman’s skill set underneath. Roman Wilson rounds out the receiving group and the Steelers also have two solid tight ends in Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. The concern here isn’t the talent, it’s improving on a passing game that was 21st in success rate and 16th in EPA per play last season. The QB situation is the same, so we’ll see if Mike McCarthy and Rodgers can improve on last year’s numbers. DEFENSE The defense remains the backbone of this team despite Mike Tomlin’s departure. Cornerback Jamel Dean will be a nice addition to the secondary, which already added Jalen Ramsey via trade last season. Dean arrives on the second-largest free agent contract in franchise history. The defense is now looking stacked, with Alex Highsmith leading the pass rush, alongside Cam Heyward, TJ Watt and Patrick Queen. This defense was what won the Steelers their division last season and they’ve arguably improved. They’ll be the key once again to masking some of their offensive limitations. PREDICTIONS 8-9 I think it’ll be a year of slight regression for the Steelers. They have a decent roster and their defense is always scary, but Mike Tomlin is gone and it’s a period of change. teams.full_text: BUFFALO BILLS | Cody Brown’s NFL Betting Guide Skip to team overview Cody Brown’s NFL BETTING GUIDE Search teams Back to all teams BUFFALO BILLS OVERVIEW The Bills enter a new era with Joe Brady replacing Sean McDermott as head coach and Jim Leonhard taking over as defensive coordinator. Buffalo's biggest move was trading for receiver DJ Moore, giving Josh Allen a true WR1, while also bolstering their defense with edge rusher Bradley Chubb and several secondary additions. Last season, the Bills had the NFL's best rushing attack, led by James Cook's league-leading 1,621 yards, but their run defense ranked among the league's worst. Allen remains an MVP-caliber dual-threat quarterback, though his passing numbers have dipped over the past two seasons. With Moore now in the mix alongside Khalil Shakir and Dalton Kincaid, and defensive upgrades aimed at fixing their run-stopping issues, Buffalo looks poised to compete for Super Bowl glory. Head Coach JOE BRADY Offensive Coordinator PETE CARMICHAEL Defensive Coordinator JIM LEONHARD OFF SEASON CHANGES It’s a new era in Buffalo after the Bills moved on from head coach Sean McDermott, replacing him with last year’s OC, Joe Brady. They also have a new defensive coordinator in Jim Leonhard (previously at Denver). The big player move was giving up a second-round pick for wide receiver DJ Moore. He’s the best receiver Josh Allen has had since Stefon Diggs left two seasons ago. Buffalo also made some defensive signings, adding edge rusher Bradley Chubb, cornerback Dee Alford and safeties C.J Gardner-Johnson and Geno Stone. Two of their top draft picks (T.J Parker and Davison Igbinosun) also bolster their defense. QUARTERBACKS Josh Allen is arguably the best quarterback in the NFL and is still just 30 years old. He’s been top-5 in MVP voting for five straight seasons and I can’t see that changing this year. He’s coming off a 25 touchdown, 10 interception season but the Bills were really lacking in top receivers. Finally they’ve given him a WR1 in DJ Moore who had a decent season in Chicago but still has plenty left in the tank. Allen is a true dual-threat QB, adding 14 rushing touchdowns and 579 rushing yards last year too. The Bills will probably want to rely less on his rushing ability this season and let him throw the ball more. He’s had two straight seasons throwing for less than 4000 yards after passing for 4000+ in the previous four seasons. His passing line is set at 3600.5 this year and if he stays healthy he should be surpassing that. RUNNING BACKS The Bills boasted the best rushing attack in the NFL in 2025, with nearly 160 yards per game. James Cook had an amazing season, leading the NFL in rushing yards with 1621. He had nine games of 100+ rushing yards and added 12 rushing TDs. It’s a seriously potent rushing attack with Josh Allen always a threat with his legs, complemented by the speed and agility of Cook. Cook got paid last year and remains the workhorse RB1 ahead of Ray Davis and Ty Johnson. There has been quite a lot of chat from training camp that Cook will be more involved in the passing game this season, which is exciting news for fantasy coaches. If he can retain that elite rushing output and also add more pass catching he will elevate himself to one of the top running backs in the NFL. RECEIVERS The Bills have a decent three-man wide receiver rotation for the first time in years after adding DJ Moore. Khalil Shakir had a solid season in 2025 with 719 receiving yards but he’s not really a first option receiver. Keon Coleman is a former second-round pick but just hasn’t delivered on his potential so far. He had 112 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 last year, but then never had a game with more than 49 yards after that point. He was also a healthy scratch for a couple of games as the Bills lost trust in him. DJ Moore is going to be crucial for Allen but it remains to be seen if he’s a complete fix to their passing game problems. Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox are great options at tight end, I’m a big fan of Kincaid especially who looks to be healthier coming into this season. DEFENSE The Bills had a great rushing attack, but their rushing defense was in the bottom-five, allowing 5 yards per carry. Their secondary was elite, allowing the fewest passing yards per game (156.9) but part of that was because teams knew they could run all over them. Jim Leonhard’s 3-4 scheme was elite against the run in Denver and he has a big task to improve Buffalo’s run defense this season. Bradley Chubb and second-round rookie TJ Parker should improve the pass rush as well, while Ed Oliver anchors the interior after an injury-shortened 2025. PREDICTIONS 11-6 I have the Bills marginally winning the AFC East. Josh Allen can win games on his own talent and they’ve added a few nice pieces for him to improve. If their run defense tightens up and DJ Moore performs, they should be a challenger for the Super Bowl. With the Bills expected to be good again, Cook should get plenty of opportunities at the goal line. He had a very impressive start for the Packers against the Ravens last season with 288 passing yards, 1 TD as well as 60 rushing yards and 2 rushing TDs. That showed his potential and he’s a nice fit for this Dolphins team who don’t really have any top receivers left to throw to. Quinn Ewers is Willis’ backup but he’s just not very good, with 3 TDs and 3 interceptions in his four appearances last season. RUNNING BACKS De’Von Achane is the Dolphins’ best offensive player and I am a really big fan of his. He’s coming off a season with 1350 rushing yards and 488 receiving yards, which are amazing numbers playing for a bad team. He’s a great option for the Dolphins but his ceiling will be limited again due to their lack of general offense. The backups are Jaylen Wright, also an explosive runner, and Ollie Gordon II who was used as the short-yardage and goal-line back at some points last season. Maye put up serious numbers: 4394 passing yards, 31 touchdowns, 450 rushing yards and just 8 interceptions. Maye is a threat with his legs too and if he can improve again this season, he will cement himself as one of the best players in the league. It will be great to see how he goes with AJ Brown, who will undoubtedly expect a lot of targets. One of the Patriots’ strengths last season was their ability to spread the ball out between receivers. He showed his ceiling in a couple of games last year, with two performances of 140+ rushing yards and 2+ touchdowns. Stevenson is the bigger back and can be used on short yardage situations, but Henderson is much more explosive and also arguably a better pass-catcher. Mike Vrabel does like to run with the hot hand at times so expect to see both guys put up decent numbers this season. He’s a former second-round pick and I still think he has plenty of potential. They ranked 25th in total defense and that was a clear focus to improve on this season. The arrivals of veterans Demario Davis and Minkah Fitzpatrick should help, plus pick 2 David Bailey who helps the pass-rush alongside Will McDonald IV. Head coach Aaron Glenn is a defensive minded coach and he’s under some pressure this year to make the scheme click. Surely we see a few more interceptions from the Jets this year… PREDICTIONS 2-15 Look away Jets fans. Whilst this is the equal worst record I have predicted for any team this season, I think there will be some positives. They’ve drafted some nice talent and this is clearly a bridge year before hopefully drafting a good quarterback at the end of the season. The offensive line has been a big problem for the last couple of years, with Stroud taking 38, 52 and 23 sacks in his first three seasons. The 23 sacks he took last season were actually the equal fewest in the league, but we could see Stroud was just trying to get the ball out as quick as possible. We saw Stroud’s issues come to a head in the postseason, where he threw five interceptions and lost five fumbles in just two games. The Texans have bolstered the offensive line and added a really good veteran RB in David Montgomery to help Stroud get his confidence back. Davis Mills will continue to be the backup and he’s entering his sixth season with the team. RUNNING BACKS The Texans had a very average run game last season and they sorely missed Joe Mixon who missed the year through injury. Mixon has now been released and the Texans signed David Montgomery who has been a great player for the Lions over the past three years. Monty had 700+ rushing yards and 8+ rushing touchdowns in all three seasons with the Lions and he’s still got plenty left in the tank at 29 years old. The Texans have made it clear they want to lean on the run and Montgomery is a bulldozing player who suits them well. He’ll form a partnership with Woody Marks who had 703 rushing yards in his first NFL season, but wasn’t efficient at just 3.6 yards per carry. They’ll be hoping he can go to new heights this year with an offense that remains largely the same. His passing yards line for the season is just 3750.5, a number that he has easily cleared in three of his five NFL seasons. He finished dead last in EPA per dropback among qualifying quarterbacks. The front office responded by hiring Robert Saleh as head coach and Brian Daboll as offensive coordinator, then spent the fourth overall pick on receiver Carnell Tate and $70 million on free agent Wan'Dale Robinson to give Ward real weapons. QUARTERBACKS Cam Ward's rookie season was rough on paper: 3169 yards, 15 touchdowns, seven interceptions, sacked a league-high 55 times. He also finished 35th of 35 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. However, he notably improved once Brian Callahan was fired and stopped calling plays. Ward flashed real toughness, starting every game despite the punishment he took. New offensive coordinator Brian Daboll is credited with developing Josh Allen into a superstar in Buffalo. Ward clearly has the talent and potential to be great, but we’ll see if last year did any lasting damage to him. RUNNING BACKS Tony Pollard returns as the lead back after a 1082 rushing yard and 5 touchdown season. If I’m honest, those numbers flattered him a lot. He was averaging less than 4 yards per carry until he had a great stretch over the final six games of the season. Nearly half of his 1082 yards came in those final six games compared to the other half in the first 11 games. Pollard is still 29 and the Titans’ offensive line is slightly revamped, so he should produce some decent numbers. His rushing line for the season is set at 775.5 – which appears a little low to me. However we do know most of these lines are accounting for an injury happening at some point. Tyjae Spears is a solid backup and the Titans drafted RB Nicholas Singleton who could get more chances as the season goes on. RECEIVERS Carnell Tate arrives via the fourth overall pick after an 875-yard, nine-touchdown junior season at Ohio State. He’s obviously a major talent and it’s rare for wide receivers to go that early in the draft. The Titans will hope he and Ward form a great partnership for years to come. All reports from camp are that he will immediately be WR1 and he looks really sharp, but there might be some growing pains with the two of them. Wan'Dale Robinson joins as a $70 million free agent after topping 1000 receiving yards with Jaxson Dart in New York. The front office added John Franklin-Myers, Alontae Taylor, and Cor'Dale Flott to patch the secondary, but this remains a unit in transition as Saleh installs his system. I think we can expect a pretty solid defensive unit, but this team probably won’t challenge for playoffs, especially in a strong AFC South. He’s currently the 15th favorite at +3000 which seems a little crazy to me… Especially seeing as I have the Broncos winning this division. Value play for you there. teams.full_text: DETROIT LIONS | Cody Brown’s NFL Betting Guide Skip to team overview Cody Brown’s NFL BETTING GUIDE Search teams Back to all teams DETROIT LIONS OVERVIEW The Lions are expected to bounce back after a difficult 2025 season where they missed the playoffs and dealt with a bad run of injuries. They have already been dealing with a few defensive injuries through preseason but their offense is looking good, with tight end Sam LaPorta looking back to fitness. RB Jahmyr Gibbs is one of the best players in the league and just signed an extension to make him the highest paid RB in history. Jared Goff has been a consistent performer for years and is still in his prime at 31 years old. The Lions have one of the easiest schedules in the league and should be a real force, I expect them to challenge for the NFC North title at least. Head Coach DAN CAMPBELL Offensive Coordinator DREW PETZING Defensive Coordinator KELVIN SHEPPARD OFF SEASON CHANGES Detroit missed the playoffs after losing both coordinators, Ben Johnson (to Chicago as head coach) and Aaron Glenn (to the Jets as head coach), and the offense noticeably slipped without Johnson calling plays, even though it still finished fourth in points and fifth in yards. The front office responded with a full offensive line overhaul after center Frank Ragnow's abrupt retirement, parting ways with longtime left tackle Taylor Decker, and hiring Drew Petzing as the new offensive coordinator while promoting Kelvin Sheppard into his second year running the defense. They also lost RB David Montgomery and replaced him with former Chief Isiah Pacheco. QUARTERBACKS Jared Goff finished second in the NFL in passing yards (4,564) and touchdowns (34), third in passer rating (105.5), and earned his fifth Pro Bowl nod despite the coordinator turnover. He’s been a very good quarterback for years now and has three straight seasons with 30+ passing touchdowns. His passing TDs line for this season is set at 29.5, a number he should go over again if he’s healthy all season. His passing yards line is set at 4050.5, also a number he has cleared in four straight seasons. RUNNING BACKS We could be about to see a historic season for Jahmyr Gibbs. He has just signed the most expensive contract in running back history worth over $25 million per season. Now that David Montgomery is gone, this is Gibbs’ backfield to dominate. In six career games without Monty, Gibbs averages 111 rushing yards and 1.2 rushing touchdowns per game. For all of us fantasy players, he averages 27.4 PPR points in games without Monty. I know Isiah Pacheco has been signed as backup, but he’s not the same player as David Montgomery. Pacheco left the Chiefs after four seasons there – he had 830+ rushing yards in his first two seasons but then followed it with just 310 and 462 rushing yards the last two years. He dealt with injuries and doesn’t look like the player he once was. With all that in mind, we can expect a massive season for Gibbs as the leader of the backfield. RECEIVERS Amon-Ra St Brown is one of the safest floor receivers in the league, with three consecutive seasons of 115+ receptions and 1250+ yards. He’s also a beast in the end zone with 10+ receiving touchdowns in three straight campaigns. I don’t see that changing this year and you can get him at decent odds for 10+ touchdowns once again. Amon-Ra rarely misses games and he’s an incredibly reliable option for Jared Goff. Expect similar numbers once again in 2026. I like him to have 10+ receiving touchdowns at +100. Jameson Williams is a nice complement to Amon-Ra, he also had over 1000 yards last season to make it back to back 1000+ seasons. Williams loves to get behind defenses and is always a threat with the deep ball. Sam LaPorta is also a great receiving option when healthy, so there's plenty of mouths to feed for Goff. DEFENSE Aidan Hutchinson led the league in pressures despite battling injuries around him, and this defense ranked 32nd in defensive player health last season — an almost unfathomable amount of bad luck. Brian Branch's Achilles tear and Kerby Joseph's knee injury both linger into 2026. Free-agent additions Chuck Clark and Christian Izien project to fill in, but better health alone could be the single biggest defensive upgrade available to Detroit this season. PREDICTIONS 11-6 The Lions have one of the easier schedules in the NFL, despite having a tough division. Their offense is extremely powerful and Jahmyr Gibbs could produce a massive season. If their defense holds up, they should return to the playoffs. FAVORITE FUTURE AMON-RA 10+ RECEIVING TOUCHDOWNS The Sun God has three straight seasons with 10+ receiving touchdowns and I don’t see that changing. The Lions have an easy schedule and are expected to be one of the highest scoring offenses in the NFL. Amon-Ra gets great separation and is one of the league leaders in red zone targets. I’m looking forward to seeing him use his legs more now that he’s another year removed from the ACL injury he suffered in 2022. George Pickens was brought back and most of the offense remains the same. The offense definitely wasn’t the problem and it’s no wonder the front office has run it back this year. Dak has some elite weapons in CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Jake Ferguson. If Dak can put together another healthy season there is no reason why he won’t be top-5 in the NFL for passing yards again. He was just overtaken by Matthew Stafford in the final week last year for most passing yards in the regular season. RUNNING BACKS Javonte Williams rejuvenated the run game on a prove-it deal last year. He recorded 1201 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, proving to be a great pickup after a couple of years of poor rushing efficiency. I expect another strong season for him in 2026 alongside a passing game that will take a lot of attention away from him. Dallas was ninth in offensive health last season with Prescott, Pickens, and Ferguson all avoiding missed games. This remains one of the most explosive, and healthiest, offenses in the NFC even without major additions this offseason. RECEIVERS George Pickens proved to be exactly the difference-maker Dallas envisioned, hauling in 93 passes for 1429 yards, third-most in the NFL, and nine touchdowns in his first season with Prescott, forcing defenses off CeeDee Lamb for the first time in years. Dallas' potent offense still left real meat on the bone, ranking just 18th in red-zone touchdown rate (56.9%) despite that bevy of weapons, suggesting there's another gear available here. teams.full_text: NEW ORLEANS SAINTS | Cody Brown’s NFL Betting Guide Skip to team overview Cody Brown’s NFL BETTING GUIDE Search teams Back to all teams NEW ORLEANS SAINTS OVERVIEW The Saints look like a genuine dark-horse in a wide-open NFC South, boosted by one of the league's easiest schedules and real momentum after Tyler Shough led them to a 4-1 finish last season. This offseason, New Orleans signed running back Travis Etienne and drafted receiver Jordyn Tyson to fully arm Shough heading into his first year as unquestioned starter. Tyson is set to miss time to start the season due to a training camp injury. Chris Olave remains the top target after a strong 1163-yard season. Defensively, losing veterans Demario Davis and Cam Jordan hurts, though new additions aim to shore up the run defense. Head Coach KELLEN MOORE Offensive Coordinator DOUG NUSSMEIER Defensive Coordinator BRANDON STALEY OFF SEASON CHANGES The front office signed running back Travis Etienne and drafted Jordyn Tyson in round one to fully arm Shough for his first year as the unquestioned starter. Tyson is a wide receiver taken at pick 8 who recorded 711 yards and 8 touchdowns in his final college season with Arizona State. The Saints also added tight end Noah Fant, punter Ryan Wright, DT John Ridgeway, Guard David Edwards and LB Kaden Elliss who is a nice replacement for Demario Davis. QUARTERBACKS The Saints look to have found a really solid QB in Tyler Shough. In the last five games of 2025 he led the Saints to a 4-1 record and threw 5 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions. That was all with very limited receiving options, something the Saints have tried to fix over the off-season. Shough’s rookie year ranked 23rd of 33 qualified quarterbacks in EPA per play and 20th in success rate, but again that was with a very weak receiving corps minus Chris Olave. He’s got rookie Jordyn Tyson to pair with Olave now and I’m quite bullish on how the Saints will go this year, especially in a weak division. RUNNING BACKS Travis Etienne arrives from Jacksonville to pair with a full offseason of continuity under Kellen Moore, though he was 27th in yards per carry among qualified backs last year — an upgrade in name more than pure efficiency for this backfield. Alvin Kamara is still a Saint but is definitely showing signs of regression – he averaged just 3.6 yards per carry last season and only added 186 receiving yards – both career lows. Etienne will be the lead back especially with Kamara dealing with an injury to start the season. RECEIVERS Chris Olave caught 100 passes for 1163 yards and 9 touchdowns despite a shaky supporting cast, and first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson joins alongside third-round tight end Oscar Delp and additional Day 3 skill-position picks. Tyson looks like a real talent and showed some great signs throughout training camp before his injury. Tight end Juwan Johnson is also a nice piece in the passing game. New Orleans was 23rd in the rate of plays gaining 10-plus yards and dead last in 20-plus-yard plays last season, a genuine big-play drought this draft class was built specifically to fix. However they have lost some crucial components of the defense in Demario Davis and Cam Jordan, both 37-year-old free agents, needing new additions like defensive tackle Christen Miller to bolster the run defense and replace real leadership and production up front this season. If Shough can build on his strong rookie season then they are a big chance to win more games again. Tyson is an exciting rookie and Travis Etienne should be a good addition at running back too. He signed a new one year deal to return and it’s clear he really wants another Super Bowl before retiring. He’s got all the weapons around him to do that with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams his key targets to throw to. Add Colby Parkinson at tight end and two really good running backs and this roster clearly has the talent to go all the way. Stafford still has an absolute arm on him and he should be competing for MVP once again if this team performs as well as expected. Kyren Williams has been elite over the past three seasons, with 10+ rushing touchdowns and 1100+ rushing yards in all three seasons. He certainly hasn’t done anything wrong, but Blake Corum has earned himself more time on the field with his performances too. Corum averaged 5.1 yards per carry last season and added 6 rushing touchdowns as well. Coach Sean McVay has said throughout pre-season that both guys will get plenty of touches. They have a great roster and are well coached but they have been dealing with some serious injury issues over the last few seasons. The electrical substation stuff is crazy to me bit there is no denying they’ve got some sort of injury curse. San Francisco's offense ranked third in success rate and sixth in points per drive last season despite Brock Purdy missing eight total games to injury, and George Kittle, Ricky Pearsall, and Jauan Jennings all missing significant time too. The front office responded by replacing Jennings with six-time Pro Bowler Mike Evans, signed to a genuinely team-friendly contract this offseason. The 49ers were one of four teams with a perfect win percentage when leading at halftime last season. Head Coach KYLE SHANAHAN Offensive Coordinator KLAY KUBIAK Defensive Coordinator RAHEEM MORRIS OFF SEASON CHANGES The big story throughout the offseason for the Niners has been their injuries. Wide Receiver Ricky Pearsall will miss the entire season after having surgery on a PCL injury that he sustained last year. It’s crazy to me that they didn’t operate on it earlier and when he arrived at training camp he was not healthy. The Niners signed future hall of famer Mike Evans but he has also been dealing with a quad strain and sat out parts of training camp. They brought back Deebo Samuel after he had a year in Washington and he’s now essential depth. WR Brandon Aiyuk is technically still with the Niners but he won’t play with them again. QUARTERBACKS Brock Purdy ranks second in the NFL in passer rating among quarterbacks with 1000-plus attempts since 2022 and when healthy in 2025 he completed 70.6% of his passes for a 7.6% touchdown rate, both elite marks even in a season limited to nine total games. He has his doubters but is definitely one of the more reliable quarterbacks in the league when healthy. Mike Evans is going to give him a really nice end zone option to complement Christian McCaffrey on the ground. Purdy’s passing touchdowns line is set for 27.5 this season which I think looks a little high. Yes, he has Evans and Deebo Samuel back, but he’s only gone above that number once in his four NFL seasons. RUNNING BACKS Christian McCaffrey returns for his 11th NFL season and looks as fit as ever. He did have some regression last season in terms of yards per carry, averaging just 3.9 YPC, his lowest mark since his first NFL season. A lot of that came down to some offensive line troubles and other health issues. I actually think despite his age he can improve that efficiency this season. His pass catching numbers are unbelievable, recording 102 receptions as a running back last year. He can do it all and I expect another productive season for him if he remains healthy. RECEIVERS If healthy, this wide receiving corps would be one of the best in the league. Unfortunately that’s not the case. Ricky Pearsall will miss the entire season through injury and new signing Mike Evans is also dealing with a quad strain. The Niners hope he’ll be ready for Week 1 though. Jauan Jennings was a sizeable loss but they replaced him with Deebo Samuel who returns for a second stint in San Francisco. The big one that the Niners are most excited about, and reliant on, is rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling. He was taken with pick 33 and has looked really good throughout preseason. George Kittle remains an elite tight end but is coming off a torn achilles and he isn’t getting any younger. He should be ready to go Week 1 but whether he can get back to his best remains to be seen. San Francisco's offense ranked third in success rate and sixth in points per drive last season even without player health, so there’s definitely upside with Purdy under center. DEFENSE Nick Bosa remains one of the NFL's premier edge defenders, and the front office added interior disruptor Osa Odighizuwa via trade to take pressure off him, while Fred Warner continues to anchor one of the league's smartest linebacker units. San Francisco was 28th in defensive player health last season, with Bosa suffering a season-ending injury in Week 3 and Warner playing just six games — better health alone could be a massive defensive upgrade. PREDICTIONS 10-7 If healthy, this team is a real playoff contender. Unfortunately there is just too much unknown for me to give them a better record. Christian McCaffrey, Brock Purdy, Mike Evans and co give them a great offensive core but all of them have injury history. This division is incredibly tough as well with the Rams and Seahawks to play twice. He might not get his usual 1000+ yardage season but he will be on the field in red zone scenarios and that’s the type of receiver the Niners have been missing. This offseason brought natural fallout, most notably losing Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker and offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, who left for the Raiders’ head-coaching job. Rookie Jadarian Price steps into the backfield to replace Walker, while Jaxon Smith- Njigba returns after winning Offensive Player of the Year. Only two franchises this century have repeated, and while Seattle’s continuity gives them a real shot, I think it will be really tough for them to repeat. Head Coach MIKE MACDONALD Offensive Coordinator BRIAN FLEURY Defensive Coordinator ADEN DURDE OFF SEASON CHANGES The offseason brought the natural fallout that follows any title team: five members of the 2022 draft class departed this offseason, most notably Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker, and offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak left for the Raiders' head-coaching job. The Seahawks drafted RB Jadarian Price in the firstround to replace Walker and they also have George Holani as RB depth. Zach Charbonnet will return at some point this season too. Seattle retained its two most important pieces, Darnold and the core of its historically great defense. QUARTERBACKS Sam Darnold completed one of the most remarkable career turnarounds in recent NFL history leading the Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory against the Patriots last season. He formed an unbelievable partnership with Jaxon Smith-Njigba last year who won Offensive Player of the Year. Seattle was third in scoring offense (28.4 points per game) last season, though only ninth in offensive success rate and 18th in EPA per play, a genuinely big-play-dependent formula. Darnold can’t be doubted anymore after winning the Super Bowl, but he’s still not considered in the top quarterbacks in the league in terms of pure talent. He averaged 238 passing yards per game last season and most of those went to JSN. It’ll be interesting to see if he spreads the ball more this season. RUNNING BACKS This is an interesting RB room with Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker leaving in free agency to the Chiefs and Zach Charbonnet still recovering from a season ending injury suffered last year. The Seahawks drafted RB Jadarian Price with the final pick of the first round and they have high hopes for him to step into a big role immediately. He should get plenty of opportunity from Week 1 and I don’t mind him at +650 for Offensive Rookie of the Year. George Holani will likely be RB2 to start the season but once Zach Charbonnet is cleared for a return he will have a prominent role in the offense too. It’s a high powered offense but the RB room feels weaker this season than it was in their Super Bowl winning season. RECEIVERS Jaxon Smith-Njigba was named 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year after leading the league in receiving yards, and Cooper Kupp returns as a complementary veteran target behind him. Rashid Shaheed was re-signed for $17 million per year and I expect him to move above Kupp in the pecking order this season. That gives Darnold a genuinely deep group to work with in year two of this partnership. Seattle ranked fourth in 20-plus-yard play rate and fifth in 10-plus-yard play rate last season, an explosive, if slightly boom-or-bust, identity that fits Darnold's aggressive downfield style well. Shaheed is a great deep threat and I can’t believe his receiving line for the season is only 500.5 yards. This passing game's continuity into year two, after a title-winning first season together, should only help this already explosive unit take another real step forward. DEFENSE Mike Macdonald's defense was the No. 1 unit in the NFL during the championship run, per Sharp ranking first in points allowed per drive, first in explosive-play rate allowed, and second in yards allowed per play. Losing edge rusher Boye Mafe to Cincinnati in free agency is a real subtraction, but Leonard Williams, DeMarcus Lawrence, and All-Pro cornerback Devon Witherspoon anchor a unit that returns largely intact into this title defense. PREDICTIONS 13-4 I have the Seahawks challenging again for the Super Bowl and NFC West. This team has an incredible defense, most of which they kept since last year. I do think JSN will be clamped up a little more and the loss of Klint Kubiak will hurt their offense too. It’s a well rounded team that should challenge, but I don’t think they will go back to back.
